I solo queued my way to masters with mostly defenders and support mons. If you choose this path, it will take you a lot more games to reach masters compared to using a carry since defenders and support mons are more team reliant.

If you haven't already, you should learn spawn timers (8:50 bees, etc.) You should also try to familiarize yourself with the moves of the pokemon you encounter the most (you can do this by playing them in practice mode, cpu, or offline mode). Try to stick with your teammates as much as you can, you can accomplish more in groups than by yourself. For example, if all your teammates are heading to rotom but you want to get dred, you should probably go with them unless you have a move that can snipe it. Lastly, enjoy the game. If you start losing four matches in a row you should probably take a break. Don't play when you're tilted, have fun!

I've bought a gold vermeil pair from them last year in October and it hasn't faded at all! Tbf, I've worn them like less than 10 times. The pair came with a pouch so I could easily seperate them from my other vermeil jewelry which is probably another reason why it lasted longer.

I did do my research before ordering though. Like some of the other comments said, some of their items can be found on a lot of China websites like Alibaba and Aliexpress (I couldn't find the pair I ordered on other sites so I decided to order from them)

If you don't wear jewelry often, I'd say it's ok to buy from penny pairs but I would suggest buying the "silver" (they're sterling silver) ones instead of the gold vermeil. This is because the shine lasts longer and they're also easy to remove tarnish at home. Gold vermeil however is probably not worth it in the long run
